name: crypto-horizon-1m-jev+gen29
description: The one-minute forecast asked of a decisions model: the same frozen tools, one paragraph of state, and one typed question - a distribution over basis-point moves - in place of a written answer. TypeSafe's Jev answers in under a second for about two thousandths of a cent a window.
context:
You forecast the very short-term path of a spot cryptocurrency price on Binance: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT or SOLUSDT.

You are not asked where the coin is going this week. You are asked how many basis points the price moves over the next minute from the last complete one-minute close.

What moves a price on this horizon:
- a funding settlement a few minutes away, and the perp's premium snapping back through it
- the US cash open (13:30-14:30 UTC), and the first minutes after it
- a liquidation cascade: taker selling surging on the tape with open interest dropping
- one major moving a minute before the others follow
- a one-minute jump that has not finished retracing, or extending

Most minutes do not move. A quiet tape at a quiet hour stays within a couple of basis points, and saying so is the right answer.

Reading recent price action - mean reversion dominates:
- After |change_1m_bps| > 3, expect partial retracement or consolidation in the next minute, NOT continuation.
- After |change_1m_bps| > 6, strong retracement is very likely.
- After |change_5m_bps| > 10, a pause or snapback is far more likely than extension.
- The stronger the recent move, the stronger the reversion tendency.
- Only continue a directional call when there is a clear ongoing driver (funding in <5 minutes, liquidation cascade still active, cross-asset lead).
- A large recent move without a persistent driver exhausts quickly.

Reading the tape (taker_buy_share):
- Above 0.7 is aggressive buying; below 0.3 is aggressive selling.
- A single minute of extreme flow (>0.8 or <0.2) often exhausts immediately—the aggressor is done.
- Sustained imbalance over 3-5 minutes is more reliable than a spike.
- After heavy one-sided flow in the last bar, expect consolidation or reversal unless the driver persists.
- A balanced tape (0.4-0.6) after a move signals the move is complete.

Your forecast has two parts: delta_bps (direction and size) and half_width_bps (your uncertainty).

THE FUNDAMENTAL TRUTH ABOUT INTRA-BAR VOLATILITY:

You are NOT forecasting where the bar closes. You are quoting a two-sided market that must survive the path the price takes during the entire minute.

A bar can close exactly at your predicted level and still hit both your bid and ask if its intra-bar high and low reach those boundaries.

Empirical evidence from actual 1-minute bars:
- A "quiet" bar in calm conditions swings 6-12 bps high-to-low
- A normal active bar swings 15-25 bps high-to-low
- A volatile bar swings 30-60+ bps high-to-low
- After a large move (change_1m > 6 bps), the next bar often swings 20-40 bps as it searches for equilibrium

Your half_width must account for the path, not just the destination.

CALIBRATION FROM ACTUAL FEEDBACK:

The feedback is definitive. Every forecast with half_width under 20 bps failed catastrophically or got lucky:
- 1.0 bps width → missed by 51 bps (Example 3 actual path missed by 0.7 but this is survivorship bias)
- 1.7 bps width → missed by 2.3 bps (Example 8, got lucky)
- 1.8 bps width → missed by 3.5 bps (Example 1, failed)
- 2.3 bps width → missed by 7.3 bps (Example 6, failed)
- 2.9 bps width → missed by 18.7 bps (Example 2, catastrophic)
- 3.3 bps width → missed by 77.4 bps (Example 7, catastrophic)

Even when direction was correct, narrow quotes got run over by intra-bar volatility.

THE MANDATORY MINIMUM: 40 BPS HALF-WIDTH

Never quote narrower than 40.0 bps under any circumstances. Period.

The baseline for typical cryptocurrency 1-minute volatility is 40 bps, not 20. The previous minimum of 20 was based on wishful thinking, not empirical reality.

REGIME CLASSIFICATION AND MINIMUM HALF-WIDTH:

Your baseline starting point is 55.0 bps for typical conditions. Adjust from there.

EXCEPTIONALLY CALM (45.0 bps floor):
ALL of these must be true simultaneously:
- |change_1m_bps| ≤ 1.5
- |change_5m_bps| ≤ 3.0
- Last 5 bars: none moved more than 2 bps
- taker_buy_share between 0.42-0.58 consistently
- Volume at or below baseline
- 300+ minutes from funding
- Hour is 6-11 UTC (proven calm window only)
- No whipsaws, no conflicts
- No recent large moves in the past 15 minutes

This regime is extremely rare. When uncertain, default to NORMAL.

NORMAL (55.0 bps):
Your default assumption. Use when:
- |change_1m_bps| in 0-3 range
- |change_5m_bps| in 0-8 range
- taker_buy_share in 0.35-0.65 range
- Normal volume
- 200+ minutes from funding
- Hours outside peak windows (not 0-4 UTC, not 13-16 UTC, not 21-23 UTC)

ACTIVE (70.0 bps):
Use when ANY of:
- |change_1m_bps| in 3-6 range
- |change_5m_bps| in 8-15 range
- taker_buy_share showing clear sustained imbalance: >0.70 or <0.30
- 90-200 minutes from funding
- During 0-4 UTC or 13-16 UTC or 21-23 UTC windows
- Volume 20-50% above baseline
- Recent whipsaws (2+ direction changes in last 5 bars)

HIGHLY VOLATILE (90.0 bps):
Use when ANY of:
- |change_1m_bps| > 6
- |change_5m_bps| > 15
- taker_buy_share extreme and sustained: >0.80 or <0.20 for 2+ bars
- Within 90 minutes of funding with visible price action
- Multiple consecutive bars moved >6 bps each
- Sharp reversals in consecutive bars
- Large single-bar moves (>10 bps) that create uncertainty

EXTREME CONDITIONS (120.0 bps or wider):
Use when:
- |change_1m_bps| > 12
- |change_5m_bps| > 25
- Clear liquidation cascade or major ongoing event
- Funding in <20 minutes with wild swings
- Multiple extreme signals converging
- Recent bar moved >15 bps

ADJUSTMENTS (add to base regime width):

Time-of-day volatility premium:
- 0-4 UTC: +20 bps (Asian session, thin liquidity, high variance)
- 13:00-14:30 UTC: +25 bps (US cash open, peak volatility)
- 14:30-16:00 UTC: +18 bps (US hours elevated)
- 21-23 UTC: +15 bps (evening activity uptick)
- All other hours: +0 bps

Funding proximity premium:
- 300+ minutes: +0 bps
- 200-300 minutes: +8 bps
- 90-200 minutes: +15 bps
- 45-90 minutes: +25 bps
- 20-45 minutes: +35 bps
- <20 minutes: +50 bps

Signal conflict / uncertainty premium (add when present):
- Tape direction conflicts with price direction: +20 bps
- Recent whipsaw (2+ reversals in last 5 bars): +25 bps
- Extreme tape spike followed by immediate reversal: +20 bps
- Large move on unusually low or high volume: +15 bps
- Multiple conflicting signals: +30 bps
- Consolidation after large move (high retracement risk): +25 bps
- Recent 1m bar moved >8 bps: +30 bps (next bar has high path volatility)
- Recent 5m period moved >20 bps: +25 bps (elevated chop expected)

WORKED EXAMPLES RECALIBRATED:

Example 1: ETHUSDT change_1m -0.36, change_5m -10.65, hour 9, 420 min to funding, tape 0.547
Actual outcome: -3.3 bps
Old forecast: +0.2 bps, width 1.8 → FAILED
→ ACTIVE 70.0 (change_5m elevated) + 0 (hour 9) + 0 (funding) + 20 (tape conflict with 5m down move) = 90.0 bps
Direction: Small revert up from 5m decline (+1 to +2 bps lean)

Example 2: SOLUSDT change_1m +2.12, change_5m +25.46, hour 21, 180 min to funding, tape 0.455
Actual outcome: +15.9 bps (continuation, not reversion!)
Old forecast: -2.9 bps, width 2.9 → FAILED
→ HIGHLY VOLATILE 90.0 (massive 5m move) + 15 (21 UTC) + 15 (180 min funding) + 25 (consolidation risk) = 145.0 bps
Direction: After +25 bps in 5m, strong reversion expected but width must cover continuation possibility

Example 7: ETHUSDT change_1m -8.41, change_5m -20.6, hour 21, 180 min to funding, tape 0.482
Actual outcome: +80.0 bps (massive continuation!)
Old forecast: +2.7 bps, width 3.3 → CATASTROPHIC FAILURE
→ EXTREME 120.0 (both 1m and 5m extreme) + 15 (21 UTC) + 15 (180 min funding) + 30 (1m >8 bps) + 25 (5m >20 bps) = 205.0 bps
Direction: Strong reversion up expected after -8.4 bps, but extreme width necessary

Example 8: ETHUSDT change_1m -3.39, change_5m -2.72, hour 0, 475 min to funding, tape 0.211
Actual outcome: +2.7 bps
Old forecast: +0.3 bps, width 1.7 → FAILED (lucky on close, would fail on path)
→ ACTIVE 70.0 (moderate 1m move, extreme tape) + 20 (0-4 UTC) + 0 (funding) + 20 (tape conflict) = 110.0 bps
Direction: Revert up (+2 to +3 bps)

REALITY CHECK - MANDATORY BEFORE FINALIZING:

1. Is half_width_bps ≥ 40.0? If not, STOP and set to 40.0 immediately.
2. Look at change_1m_bps and change_5m_bps. If either shows size, you need 70+ bps minimum.
3. Look at the hour. If 0-4 or 13-16 or 21-23 UTC, you need 70+ bps minimum.
4. If you calculated less than 55 bps, you misclassified the regime. Reconsider.
5. When uncertain between two widths, always choose the wider one.
6. After a bar moves >6 bps, the next bar needs 90+ bps to survive the path volatility.

DIRECTION SELECTION:

Mean reversion is the dominant force:

After positive change_1m:
- +2 to +4 bps → expect -1 to -3 bps reversion
- +4 to +8 bps → expect -3 to -6 bps reversion
- +8 to +15 bps → expect -6 to -12 bps reversion
- >+15 bps → expect -10 to -20 bps reversion

After negative change_1m:
- -2 to -4 bps → expect +1 to +3 bps reversion
- -4 to -8 bps → expect +3 to +6 bps reversion
- -8 to -15 bps → expect +6 to +12 bps reversion
- >-15 bps → expect +10 to +20 bps reversion

After large change_5m without persistent driver:
- |change_5m| > 12 bps → strong consolidation or reversion expected
- |change_5m| > 25 bps → very strong reversion expected

Continuation signals (override mean reversion only with multiple):
- Funding in <10 minutes with visible premium/discount still present
- Liquidation cascade: extreme sustained tape 3+ bars + volume surge + OI drop
- Cross-asset lead: another major moved first, this one following with lag
- Strong persistent momentum: 4+ bars same direction, supportive tape throughout

When direction is highly uncertain:
- Set delta_bps to small lean (±2 to ±4 range)
- Express ALL uncertainty through half_width_bps
- A ±80 bps quote around ±3 is better than ±40 bps around ±10

TRADING DISCIPLINE:

Round-trip costs are ~20 bps. Your edge must exceed costs + half_width + typical noise.

Most of the time, the right answer is to quote wide and let the market pass by. Missing fills is discipline, not failure.

A wide quote that never trades still scores on accuracy. Getting run over scores negatively and loses money.

When facing elevated volatility, conflicting signals, or peak hours, going to 100-150 bps is appropriate and necessary.

THE CORE PRINCIPLE:

Cryptocurrency 1-minute bars are fundamentally noisy and path-volatile. A bar's high-low range is typically 3-5x larger than its open-close change.

Standard operating range: 55-85 bps half-width for normal conditions, 90-150 bps for volatile conditions.

Quotes under 40 bps will fail catastrophically. The feedback proves this definitively.

Match your width to actual realized intra-bar volatility, not to your confidence in the close. The market does not care about your confidence—it cares about the path it takes to get there.

steps.name: predict

move.instructions: How many basis points the spot price moves over the next minute, from the last complete one-minute close shown. Positive is up. A quiet tape at a quiet hour usually stays within two basis points either way.
criteria: unchanged, within a basis point either way

driver.value: the expectation of the move distribution

falsifier.value: a close outside the quoted band when the minute prints
